artifacts.summary: Discriminating blocked classifier arm shipped across 8 phases: classifier mechanism, its fixtures, dry-run reason threading, both orchestrate skills, the state-machine doc, and the guardrails Gate Catalogue all converged on the narrowed premise.

completion_data.completion_summary: Replaced the multi-task /orchestrate classifier's unconditional blocked verdict with a six-branch discriminating arm so a task blocked purely on an in-batch predecessor dispatches once that predecessor completes, instead of skipping forever; propagated the change through the classifier's own tables/prose, its test fixtures (12 new RED-confirmed assertions), the dry-run report's reason threading, both orchestrate skills, the state-machine doc, and the guardrails Gate Catalogue.

memory_candidates.content: When a jq classifier's status arm needs to look up a related entity's status from the same already-slurped array (e.g. resolving a dependency's own status by project_number), bind the outer value with `. as $x` before entering a nested `select()` filter. A bare `.` inside `map({..., dep_status: (... | select(.project_number == .) ...)})` silently resolves to the INNER filter's context (the array element being tested), not the outer mapped value, causing every lookup to fail/return null with no error. Symptom: all cross-referenced lookups return the same wrong/null value regardless of input. Fix: `map(. as $d | {dep: $d, dep_status: (($all[] | select(.project_number == $d) | .status) // null)})`.

When converging a discriminating verdict from 'always skip/escalate' to 'discriminate by looking up related state', treat the discriminator as a lookup against the full already-loaded state array (not the caller's own candidate-list arguments) whenever the caller's candidate list is a shrinking, per-cycle eligibility set. A dependency that JUST became eligible for the discriminated case is, by construction, the same one that just dropped OUT of the caller's per-cycle candidate list -- so membership-based discrimination reproduces the exact defect being fixed. Verify this design guard with a fixture whose dependency is deliberately never passed as an argument to the function under test.

When adding rows to a markdown table inside a maintained context/pattern file that is tracked by a maintenance index (index-entries.json with a per-file line_count field), re-run the repo's doc-lint (check-extension-docs.sh) before considering the phase done -- a table-row addition changes the file's line count and silently drifts the index's declared value, which a downstream deploy-verification gate (Rule R) catches as a FAIL. Cheap to catch immediately; easy to miss if verification is deferred past the edit.
